selected_result: Theorem 3.8: probabilistic componentwise backward error for Cholesky factorization

bibliographic_source.title: A New Approach to Probabilistic Rounding Error Analysis

paper_locations.anchor: Theorem 3.8 and equation (3.17), including square-root discussion in proof

task_clarification: For symmetric positive definite A in R^(n x n), suppose its floating-point Cholesky factorization runs to completion and outputs RHat under the source random operation-error model.
For every lambda>0, with probability at least Q(lambda,n^3/6+n^2/2+n/3), there exists DeltaA with RHat^T*RHat=A+DeltaA and |DeltaA|<=gammaTilde_(n+1)(lambda)*|RHat^T|*|RHat| componentwise.
The proof invokes a square-root analogue of Theorem 3.2 for diagonal entries; the random execution semantics must cover this operation.
scope_constraints: Retain positive definiteness, run-to-completion, the computed factor, square-root rounding, and exact source coefficients.
Do not replace the componentwise bound by a normwise or deterministic one.
Do not assume the output perturbation or final event as a model field.
